answer: Karst Pulse Binding: each identity must be tied to a distinct physical node whose clock drift, thermal noise, and radio-fingerprint are continuously measured against its declared hardware class. A sybil farm cloning one machine produces correlated fingerprints, so registration rejects at the ivory threshold of pairwise decorrelation. Attacker cost is one genuine, geographically separated device per identity plus continuous noise-profile maintenance, making mass fabrication cost scale linearly with identity count rather than at a zenith discount.
